### Exit criteria: maximum useful lookahead depth (recall >= 0.6)

**No swept depth reaches recall >= 0.6** and holds it -- this model needs deeper lookahead than tested here, or E7's byte-reduction mechanism instead of (or in addition to) more lookahead.

> Deterministic-queue result: when rho<=1 (link keeps up), queue depth Q doesn't matter at all -- occupancy/utilization are already at their floor and nothing is ever dropped. When rho>1, a bigger Q doesn't reduce the steady-state drop rate either (it's fixed at 1-1/rho) -- it only delays how long the fill-up transient takes. **Making the prefetch buffer deeper never fixes an overloaded link** -- only more bandwidth or fewer bytes (E7) does.
